claims.quoted_text: Both caps are portions of cylinders (considering their cross-sections in the \(xy\)-plane) that are cut off by planes perpendicular to the \(z\)-axis.
claims.explanation: The cap surfaces are not portions of cylinders. For each z the cross-section is a disk of radius 1-|z|, so the bounding surfaces z=1-r and z=r-1 are conical, not cylindrical. A cylinder would have constant radius cross-sections.

claims.quoted_text: The solid formed is essentially a cylinder with height 2 (from \(z = -1\) to \(z = 1\)) minus two hemispheres (one at each end).
claims.explanation: The actual solid is a double cone, not a cylinder minus two hemispheres. At height z the cross-sectional radius is 1-|z|, so each half is a cone of radius 1 and height 1. The cylinder-minus-hemispheres model is geometrically wrong, even though it coincidentally gives the same volume.
